course_title: Introduction to Stochastic Processes with Applications

modules.purpose: Estimate quantities with random samples and see why repeated trials become more stable.
learning_objectives: Explain how repeated random samples produce a Monte Carlo estimate.
Interpret a sample mean as an estimator and compare it with a target quantity.
Relate sample size to standard error and the law of large numbers.

knowledge_points.title: Monte Carlo estimation
knowledge_points.summary: Use repeated random samples to estimate a quantity such as π.
knowledge_points.simulation_prompt: Estimate π with a Monte Carlo experiment using 10000 samples
knowledge_points.practice_prompt: Why does Monte Carlo estimation require repeated sampling?

knowledge_points.title: Sample mean
knowledge_points.summary: Interpret the sample mean as the estimator produced by repeated trials.
knowledge_points.practice_prompt: What does the sample mean estimate in a Monte Carlo experiment?

knowledge_points.title: Law of large numbers
knowledge_points.summary: Observe how an estimate stabilizes as the sample size grows.
knowledge_points.practice_prompt: How does a Monte Carlo estimate usually change as the sample size grows?

knowledge_points.title: Standard error
knowledge_points.summary: Relate sampling variability to the inverse square root of the sample size.
knowledge_points.practice_prompt: Why does quadrupling the sample size usually reduce estimation error?

modules.purpose: Model random arrivals in discrete and continuous time and connect counts with waiting times.
learning_objectives: Distinguish Bernoulli trials from Poisson arrivals.
Connect accumulated counts with binomial and Poisson distributions.
Explain geometric and exponential waiting-time behavior.

knowledge_points.title: Bernoulli process
knowledge_points.summary: Model independent arrivals in discrete time with a fixed event probability.
knowledge_points.simulation_prompt: Simulate a Bernoulli process with 100 slots, event probability 0.3, and 500 paths
knowledge_points.practice_prompt: What does each time slot represent in a Bernoulli process?

knowledge_points.title: Binomial counts
knowledge_points.summary: Compare the accumulated Bernoulli arrivals with a binomial distribution.
knowledge_points.practice_prompt: Why do Bernoulli arrivals over fixed slots follow a binomial distribution?

knowledge_points.title: Geometric waiting time
knowledge_points.summary: Study the first-arrival waiting time in a Bernoulli process.
knowledge_points.practice_prompt: How does the first-arrival waiting time change when the event probability decreases?

knowledge_points.title: Poisson process
knowledge_points.summary: Use independent increments and exponential interarrival times in continuous time.
knowledge_points.simulation_prompt: Simulate a Poisson process with rate 2, horizon 5, and 200 paths
knowledge_points.practice_prompt: Why is the mean count of a Poisson process λt?

modules.purpose: Build discrete-time walks from independent steps and study drift, variance, hitting, and absorption.
learning_objectives: Construct a random walk from up and down steps.
Relate step probabilities to endpoint drift and variance.
Interpret boundary hitting probabilities and absorption times.

knowledge_points.title: Random-walk increments
knowledge_points.summary: Build a discrete-time walk from independent up and down steps.
knowledge_points.simulation_prompt: Simulate a 100-step random walk with 500 paths and compare the theoretical mean
knowledge_points.practice_prompt: When the up-step probability is greater than 0.5, which way does the endpoint mean move?

knowledge_points.title: Drift and variance
knowledge_points.summary: Compare empirical endpoint mean and variance with their theoretical values.
knowledge_points.practice_prompt: Why do the mean and variance of a random walk depend on the number of steps?

knowledge_points.title: Hitting probability
knowledge_points.summary: Estimate the chance that a walk reaches a boundary before another boundary.
knowledge_points.practice_prompt: What do the boundaries represent in the gambler's ruin problem?

knowledge_points.title: Absorption time
knowledge_points.summary: Interpret the number of steps until a boundary is reached.
knowledge_points.practice_prompt: What factors affect the time needed for a walk to reach a boundary?

modules.purpose: Use Poisson jump times to understand random motion in continuous time.
learning_objectives: Describe how a Poisson process supplies jump times.
Read a continuous-time path between successive jumps.
Predict how the jump rate changes motion over a fixed horizon.

knowledge_points.title: Poisson jump times
knowledge_points.summary: Use Poisson arrivals as the random clock for a continuous-time walk.
knowledge_points.simulation_prompt: Simulate a continuous-time random walk with rate 2, horizon 5, and 500 paths
knowledge_points.practice_prompt: Why are the jump times random in a continuous-time random walk?

knowledge_points.title: Continuous-time sample paths
knowledge_points.summary: Interpret the path as piecewise constant between jump times.
knowledge_points.practice_prompt: Why does a continuous-time random-walk path stay constant between jumps?

knowledge_points.title: Jump-rate effects
knowledge_points.summary: Compare how the jump rate changes the number of moves in a fixed horizon.
knowledge_points.practice_prompt: How does increasing the jump rate change a path over a fixed horizon?

modules.purpose: Connect scaled random walks to Brownian motion and its Gaussian paths and distributions.
learning_objectives: Describe Brownian motion through its independent Gaussian increments.
Explain how scaling links random walks with Brownian paths.
Use the terminal distribution and sample paths to study hitting events.

knowledge_points.title: Gaussian increments
knowledge_points.summary: Study Brownian increments as independent normal random variables.
knowledge_points.simulation_prompt: Simulate Brownian motion with 500 paths, T=1, and 200 grid steps; explain the terminal variance
knowledge_points.practice_prompt: What do independent Brownian increments mean?

knowledge_points.title: Brownian scaling
knowledge_points.summary: Compare a scaled random walk with Brownian motion.
knowledge_points.practice_prompt: How does a scaled random walk approximate Brownian motion?

knowledge_points.title: Terminal distribution
knowledge_points.summary: Verify that B(T) has mean zero and variance T.
knowledge_points.practice_prompt: Why does the variance of B(T) grow linearly with T?

knowledge_points.title: Hitting events
knowledge_points.summary: Use sample paths to discuss reaching a prescribed level.
knowledge_points.practice_prompt: How do hitting-event statistics differ between one Brownian path and many paths?

modules.purpose: Represent memoryless state transitions and study long-run and absorbing behavior.
learning_objectives: Use a transition matrix to describe one-step state changes.
Apply the Markov property to separate the present from the full past.
Find and interpret stationary distributions and absorbing states.

knowledge_points.title: Transition matrix
knowledge_points.summary: Use a transition matrix to specify one-step state changes.
knowledge_points.simulation_prompt: Simulate a Markov chain for 500 steps and compare its stationary distribution
knowledge_points.practice_prompt: Why must each row of a transition matrix sum to 1?

knowledge_points.title: Markov Property
knowledge_points.summary: Explain why the next state depends on the present state rather than the full past.
knowledge_points.practice_prompt: What extra information from the past does the Markov property rule out?

knowledge_points.title: Stationary Distribution
knowledge_points.summary: Compare long-run empirical state frequencies with a stationary distribution.
knowledge_points.practice_prompt: Why does a stationary distribution satisfy πP=π?

knowledge_points.title: Absorption and gambler's ruin
knowledge_points.summary: Apply a Markov chain to absorbing boundaries and ruin events.
knowledge_points.practice_prompt: Why can an absorbing state not be left once it is reached?

modules.purpose: Describe continuous-time state changes with holding times, generators, and birth-death models.
learning_objectives: Interpret holding times and rates of leaving a state.
Read a generator matrix as a description of continuous-time transitions.
Use birth-death and reliability chains to explain state dynamics.

knowledge_points.title: Holding times
knowledge_points.summary: Describe how long a continuous-time Markov chain stays in a state.
knowledge_points.simulation_prompt: Simulate a continuous-time Markov chain with failure rate 0.25, repair rate 0.15, and horizon 200
knowledge_points.practice_prompt: How are holding times related to the rate of leaving a state?

knowledge_points.title: Generator matrix
knowledge_points.summary: Use a generator matrix to encode continuous-time transition rates.
knowledge_points.practice_prompt: Why are the diagonal entries of a generator matrix usually negative?

knowledge_points.title: Birth-death process
knowledge_points.summary: Model adjacent upward and downward transitions with birth and death rates.
knowledge_points.simulation_prompt: Simulate a birth-death process with birth rate 0.35, death rate 0.3, capacity 6, and horizon 500
knowledge_points.practice_prompt: How do birth and death rates affect the state path?

knowledge_points.title: Two-state reliability chain
knowledge_points.summary: Interpret failure and repair as a two-state continuous-time Markov chain.
knowledge_points.practice_prompt: What happens to the long-run up-state probability when the failure rate increases?

modules.purpose: Apply stochastic-process ideas to reliability, buffers, queues, and stability conditions.
learning_objectives: Relate lifetimes to survival and hazard functions.
Compare series and parallel reliability systems.
Analyze finite buffers, M/M/1 queues, and the stability condition λ<μ.

knowledge_points.title: Survival and hazard functions
knowledge_points.summary: Relate lifetimes to survival functions and hazard rates.
knowledge_points.simulation_prompt: Simulate a reliability model with component failure rates 0.8 and 1.2
knowledge_points.practice_prompt: What do the survival function and hazard rate describe?

knowledge_points.title: Series and parallel systems
knowledge_points.summary: Compare system lifetimes under series and parallel arrangements.
knowledge_points.practice_prompt: Why is the lifetime of a series system the minimum component lifetime?

knowledge_points.title: Batch buffer model
knowledge_points.summary: Track arrivals and service in a finite-capacity buffer.
knowledge_points.simulation_prompt: Simulate a buffer with arrival probability 0.6, capacity 10, 500 steps, and 200 paths
knowledge_points.practice_prompt: What trend appears when arrivals are faster than service?

knowledge_points.title: M/M/1 queue
knowledge_points.summary: Study Poisson arrivals, exponential service and the stability condition λ<μ.
knowledge_points.simulation_prompt: Simulate an M/M/1 queue with arrival rate 0.75, service rate 1, and horizon 2000
knowledge_points.practice_prompt: Why does the average queue length grow rapidly as λ approaches μ?

modules.purpose: Explore changing arrival rates with thinning and integrated intensity.
learning_objectives: Explain how a time-varying intensity differs from a fixed rate.
Use thinning to simulate candidate and accepted events.
Relate integrated intensity to the expected event count.

knowledge_points.title: Time-varying intensity
knowledge_points.summary: Describe a Poisson process whose event rate changes over time.
knowledge_points.practice_prompt: How does a time-varying intensity differ from the fixed rate of a homogeneous Poisson process?

knowledge_points.title: Thinning algorithm
knowledge_points.summary: Generate candidate events and accept them according to a time-varying rate.
knowledge_points.simulation_prompt: Simulate a nonhomogeneous Poisson process by thinning with base rate 2, peak increment 6, and peak center 13
knowledge_points.practice_prompt: Why does thinning require an upper bound on the intensity?

knowledge_points.title: Integrated intensity
knowledge_points.summary: Compare the mean count with the integral of the intensity function.
knowledge_points.practice_prompt: Why does integrated intensity give the expected event count?

modules.purpose: Study path dependence, trapping, and stopping lengths in self-avoiding walks.
learning_objectives: Describe why a self-avoiding walk depends on its visited set.
Explain how a growing path can become trapped.
Compare stopping lengths across repeated paths.

knowledge_points.title: Self-avoidance
knowledge_points.summary: Construct a walk that never revisits a previously visited site.
knowledge_points.simulation_prompt: Simulate a self-avoiding walk with maximum 1000 steps and 500 runs
knowledge_points.practice_prompt: Why can the next step of a self-avoiding walk not depend only on its current position?

knowledge_points.title: Path trapping
knowledge_points.summary: Observe that a growing path can exhaust all available neighbouring sites.
knowledge_points.practice_prompt: How can a growing path trap itself?

knowledge_points.title: Stopping length
knowledge_points.summary: Compare stopping lengths over repeated self-avoiding walks.
knowledge_points.practice_prompt: How does the empirical stopping-length distribution help explain trapping?

modules.purpose: Model particles that move and merge, then analyze cluster and coalescence times.
learning_objectives: Describe random motion of particles on a discrete circle.
Explain why coalescence can only reduce the number of clusters.
Interpret how system size and particle count affect coalescence time.

knowledge_points.title: Random particle motion
knowledge_points.summary: Move particles randomly on a discrete circle.
knowledge_points.simulation_prompt: Simulate coalescing particles on a circle of size 12 with 9 particles and 200 runs
knowledge_points.practice_prompt: How does the circle size affect the chance that particles meet?

knowledge_points.title: Coalescence
knowledge_points.summary: Merge particles when they meet and track the number of clusters.
knowledge_points.practice_prompt: Why can the number of clusters never increase during coalescence?

knowledge_points.title: Coalescence time
knowledge_points.summary: Summarize the time until all particles have merged into one cluster.
knowledge_points.practice_prompt: How might the time to complete coalescence change when the initial particle count increases?
